data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Blockchain consensus requires distributed agreement, while log commitments can be unilateral.","Blockchain immutability is enforced by economic incentives, whereas log commitments rely on cryptographic guarantees."],"overturn_conditions":["A cryptographic breakthrough renders the commitment scheme insecure.","The log's replay semantics are redefined to exclude the committed state."],"shared_structure":["Both cryptographic commitments and blockchain consensus mechanisms enforce immutability of a state.","Both rely on computational hardness to prevent retroactive changes."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_005"],"transfer_claims":["If a blockchain can turn divergence into a detectable inconsistency, a cryptographic commitment to a log can do the same."]},"claim":"A cryptographic commitment (e.g., Merkle root or digital signature) to the log's state at publication time is the sole durable binding that turns silent divergence into a contradiction.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The cryptographic primitives used are broken or compromised.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log's state is not fully captured in the commitment (e.g., missing metadata or external dependencies).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The replay environment does not enforce verification of the commitment.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log includes non-deterministic elements not covered by the commitment.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The cryptographic commitment irrevocably fixes the log's state at publication. Any divergence during replay would require altering the committed state, which is computationally infeasible without detection, thus creating a contradiction.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
